hypothesis: A five-asset shared-account canary restricted to six explicitly selected bidirectional routes may produce cleaner and more frequent forward evidence than v28's mixture of 23 executable mappings, while preserving one-position-per-asset isolation and exact backend telemetry.
decision: Retain the inactive v29 candidate and supersede only its implementation-source baseline. Revision 1's first verified bundle preceded the final route-evidence telemetry confidence normalization. Preserve that bundle, create a new independently verified bundle over the current Python source set, and bind all future transition guidance to the new implementation identity. The profile bytes, six routes, both-direction scope, risk contracts, economic confidence, and lack of live authority are unchanged.
falsifier: A mismatch in the candidate profile, current implementation source set, new backup manifest, prior-revision hash, route scope, side scope, or runtime boundary invalidates this revision. Economic falsifiers remain those declared in revision 1 and require another append-only revision rather than automatic promotion or mutation.
limitations: The new bundle is a credential-free observe-mode implementation baseline and does not replace the mandatory backup created by a later authorized live startup.
The economic evidence and low-to-medium profitability confidence remain unchanged from revision 1.
No live route, process, order, position, stop, target, or allocation changed in this revision.
